turns.en: No, but my wife, everybody's raving about it. I've been watching basketball, so I just haven't had the spare time yet. But okay.
turns.zh: 没有，不过我妻子一直在夸赞它。我一直在看篮球赛，所以暂时还没空。不过没关系。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I have a basketball question, but first of all, before we get to that, do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to find useful and work in life?
turns.zh: 我有个关于篮球的问题，不过首先，在我们讨论这个问题之前，你有没有一个自己常回味、觉得很有用、能应用到生活中的座右铭？

turns.speaker: Bob Baxley
turns.en: Yeah, so there's three quotes that I come back to all the time that I repeat in most of my talks. First one I've already used, which is, design is clear thinking made visible, by Edward Tufte. (01:35:14): Second one is from the American landscape photographer, Ansel Adams. And I've also alluded to this and the quote is, there's nothing worse than a brilliant image of a fuzzy concept. And then the last one is an African proverb and it goes like this, if you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together. (01:35:31): And I think we've touched on all three of those things today when we've talked about the resolution of comps, we've talked about using gen AI to try to go faster, things like that. And those two ideas collide in interesting way. (01:35:44): People think if they cut their colleagues out of the pie, they can go faster. And it's true, they can go faster. You just can't go very far. You need a group if you want to go far. And just because you can create a brilliant image doesn't mean you got a good concept. (01:35:58): Go look on Instagram, you'll find plenty of photographs that tingle your senses from a visual perspective and you will forget them by the time you close the app because they don't mean anything. And so we live in a time when it's very easy to produce things at incredibly high production values, but they don't mean anything. And so they're just like fancy potato chips. There's no nourishment there, man.
turns.zh: 嗯，有三个名言我经常回想，在我的大多数演讲中都会提到。第一个我已经用过了，是爱德华·塔夫特（Edward Tufte）说的，"设计就是清晰的思维具象化"。（01:35:14）第二个来自美国风景摄影师安塞尔·亚当斯（Ansel Adams），我也提过，他说："没有什么比模糊概念的精彩图像更糟糕的了。"最后一个是非洲谚语："想走得快，就独自前行；想走得远，就结伴同行。"（01:35:31）我觉得今天我们讨论了这三个方面——我们谈到了原型设计的分辨率，谈到了利用生成式人工智能来提高效率，等等。这两个观点在某种程度上产生了有趣的碰撞。（01:35:44）有些人认为，如果把同事排除在外，就能更快地前进。确实，他们能更快地行动，但走不远。想要走得远，就需要团队合作。仅仅因为能创作出精彩的图像，并不意味着你有了一个好的概念。（01:35:58）去Instagram看看，你会发现很多照片在视觉上令人惊叹，但当你关闭应用程序时，很快就会忘记它们，因为它们毫无意义。我们生活在一个可以用极高的制作水准快速产出内容的时代，但这些内容毫无意义。它们就像精美的薯片，毫无营养。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that this connects back to the vibe coding apps and prototypes that people build, but you can do it really quickly, but it won't go too far, potentially, not to hit on those tools. They're amazing.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢这与人们编写的编码应用和原型之间的联系——你可以很快完成，但可能走不远。当然，这些工具很棒。

turns.speaker: Bob Baxley
turns.en: They are. All this AI stuff is profoundly amazing and I will encourage people, one of the most amazing things for me about this moment in AI is that this, the kind of AI we're experiencing has been theorized for well over 50 years. (01:36:46): So there is a vast warehouse of interesting, amazing thoughts from philosophers and engineers and social scientists and people thinking about what is this moment going to mean when we have this sort of artificial intelligence that challenges our conception of what it means to be human. (01:37:02): So there's so much stuff you could be reading to help you process this moment in the very intense and profound psychological challenges it's bringing forth.
turns.zh: 确实如此。所有这些人工智能技术都非常令人惊叹。我要鼓励大家，在人工智能领域，当前最让我兴奋的是，我们所经历的这种人工智能理论已经被研究了50多年了。（01:36:46）因此，有大量来自哲学家、工程师、社会科学家等学者的有趣而深刻的思想，探讨当我们拥有这种挑战人类概念的AI时，它将意味着什么。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It definitely feels like we're finally living in the future. The future's actually happening. It's going to be robots walking around soon. We get self-driving cars all over San Francisco and it's really stark.
turns.zh: 确实感觉我们终于生活在未来了。未来正在发生。很快就会有机器人四处走动了。旧金山到处都是自动驾驶汽车，这真的很震撼。

turns.speaker: Bob Baxley
turns.en: It's a future. Yeah.
turns.zh: 这就是未来。是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's a future. Well, that's my concern with a lot of the fiction of the future is most of it is dystopian and here's all the problems that we're going to run into, which is going to be useful. Here's the robot laws that we got to be thinking about.
turns.zh: 这就是未来。不过，我对很多未来设想的担忧是，大多数都是反乌托邦式的，都是在预告我们即将面临的种种问题，这或许会有用。比如我们需要思考的机器人法律。

turns.speaker: Bob Baxley
turns.en: Just to go back to this idea of how once you create an expression of something, people baseline off of it. I recently got to hear Henry Modisett who's head of design at Perplexity, give a talk. And one of the things he said that just really struck me was that people's conception of AI was founded, was put out there by Hollywood years ago. (01:37:56): So this idea that AI is going to take stuff over and is ultimately really dystopian and malevolent towards humans and stuff like that, it's actually something that's created by Hollywood and now we're trying to outlive how and stuff like that. (01:38:11): And so it's just such a great example of somebody put the concept out there and planted that seed in people's heads and now we're struggling to get people off that baseline and to look at it with fresh eyes.
turns.zh: 回到这个观点：一旦你对某事物进行了表述，人们就会以此为基准线。我最近听了Perplexity公司设计总监亨利·莫迪塞特（Henry Modisett）的演讲。他说的一句话让我深有感触，那就是人们对人工智能的概念是由好莱坞多年前塑造的。（01:37:56）：所以这种认为人工智能会接管一切、最终对人类极具威胁的观念，实际上是由好莱坞创造的，而我们现在却在努力摆脱这种刻板印象，重新审视这个问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's a really good point. It's much more entertaining to watch AI try to kill us all, not just, oh, everything's amazing. Great job, AI. (01:38:34): Okay, final question. I know you're a huge sports fan. In particular, you're a big Warriors fan. So let me just ask you this. Say you were running the Warriors, the owner of the Golden State Warriors, what would you change? What would you change to help them win?
turns.zh: 这观点真不错。看着人工智能试图杀死我们所有人比“哦，一切都太棒了”要有趣多了。干得好，人工智能。（01:38:34）：好，最后一个问题。我知道你是个超级体育迷，尤其是金州勇士队的忠实粉丝。让我问你个问题。如果你来运营勇士队，成为勇士队的老板，你会做出哪些改变？怎样做才能帮助他们赢球？

turns.speaker: Bob Baxley
turns.en: A real team can't be dependent on a single player. And I think there's such a dramatic difference in the Warriors when Steph is on the court and off the court. If you listen to the local announcers, they're always like, "These non-Steph minutes really matter." (01:39:05): I look at that, I'm like, that's not really a team then, right? That's Steph in the band of Merriman. And the Warriors are bigger than that and most of these basketball teams are bigger than that currently. I think across a lot of places in the NBA, there's a single player that can go down that makes a difference in the organization's success and that just seems dangerous and not a team. (01:39:28): So I don't know what to say. I don't know how you replace Steph Curry. He is a singular, if you even call him a generational player, it's a bit bigger than that. He is unequivocally the greatest shooter in the history of the game and he's one of only two or three players has actually fundamentally changed how the game's played. (01:39:45): But I just know for winning, the Warriors are at risk because Steph is meaningfully old for an NBA player and you can't have the whole franchise built around just him.
turns.zh: 一支真正的球队不应该依赖单个球员。我觉得当斯蒂芬上场和下场时，勇士队的表现差别巨大。如果你听当地解说员的话，他们总会说：“这些非斯蒂芬的上场时间真的很重要。”（01:39:05）：我听了之后就想，这根本不算真正的球队，对吧？这就是斯蒂芬在梅里曼乐队里的表现。勇士队应该比这更强大，大多数篮球队目前也都比这更强大。NBA很多球队都有单个球员能对球队成功产生决定性影响，这实在太危险了，根本不算真正的团队。（01:39:28）：所以我不知道该怎么说。我不知道如何取代斯蒂芬·库里。他是个非凡的球员，如果你称他为一代巨星，那还远不止如此。他无疑是篮球史上最伟大的射手，也是仅有的两三位从根本上改变比赛打法的球员之一。（01:39:45）：但我知道就夺冠而言，勇士队面临风险，因为斯蒂芬的年龄对NBA球员来说实在太大了，而且球队不能完全围绕他来构建。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love this hot take. A great way to end it, Bob. I can listen to you all day. This is so fun and interesting in so many ways on so many levels. Two final questions. Where can folks find you online if they want to reach out and maybe learn more about what you're up to and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 我喜欢这种大胆的见解。鲍勃，这真是完美的收尾。我可以听你讲一整天。这在很多方面、多个层面上都非常有趣、充满乐趣。最后两个问题。如果听众想联系你，了解更多信息，或者想帮助你，他们该怎么做？

turns.speaker: Bob Baxley
turns.en: So, Bobbaxley.com is the easiest place right now. It's just a bento site, but I'll get some more stuff up there in the coming days, hopefully before this episode goes out. We'll see. (01:40:21): But there's plenty of links there that'll help you connect to me on LinkedIn and some of my talks and a few Links to some other things that I find useful. Just find me on LinkedIn. I publish pretty much every day on LinkedIn, so that's an easy way to find me. (01:40:34): I'm happy to be connected to whoever is interested in being connected.
